title: Grade 4 Math — Mon, Jun 16
description: Geometry — Day 1 of 5: Types of lines
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A straight line extends in both directions without end. How many endpoints does it have?
options: None — it goes on forever in both directions
questions.explanation: A line has no endpoints — it extends infinitely in both directions. A line segment has two endpoints.

questions.question: A line segment has:
questions.explanation: A line segment has two endpoints and a definite length. AB is a line segment from point A to point B.

questions.question: A ray has:
options: One starting point and goes on forever in one direction
questions.explanation: A ray starts at one point (the endpoint) and extends infinitely in one direction. Like a ray of light from a source.

questions.question: Parallel lines are lines that:
options: Never meet and are always the same distance apart
Cross each other at any angle
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never intersect (meet) and remain the same distance apart. Like railway tracks.

questions.question: Which is a real-life example of parallel lines?
options: The two arms of a compass
questions.explanation: Railway tracks are parallel — they never meet and stay the same distance apart.

questions.question: Perpendicular lines are lines that:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at exactly 90° (a right angle). Like the corner of a square or the letter L.

questions.question: Which is a real-life example of perpendicular lines?
options: The parallel bars in a fence
The edges of a page (where horizontal meets vertical)
questions.explanation: The edges of a page meet at 90° (right angles) — they are perpendicular to each other.

questions.question: Intersecting lines are lines that:
options: Cross (meet) each other at any angle
questions.explanation: Intersecting lines cross each other at some point. They can meet at any angle (if 90°, they are perpendicular — a special case).

questions.question: Are perpendicular lines also intersecting lines?
options: Yes — perpendicular lines intersect at 90°, which is a special case of intersecting
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines DO intersect — at a right angle. Perpendicular is a special case of intersecting.

questions.question: A curved line:
options: Is the same as a straight line
questions.explanation: A curved line bends — it is not straight. A circle, an arc, and a wavy line are all curved lines.

questions.question: Which of these is a straight line?
questions.explanation: The edge of a ruler is straight. Circles and wavy lines are curved.

questions.question: Look at the letter 'H'. What type of lines are the two vertical bars?
questions.explanation: The two vertical bars of 'H' are parallel — they never meet and are the same distance apart.

questions.question: Look at the letter 'T'. What is the relationship between the horizontal and vertical bars?
questions.explanation: In 'T', the horizontal bar sits on the vertical bar at a right angle (90°) — they are perpendicular.

questions.question: A point is:
options: An exact location in space — no size or shape
A tiny dot that has area
questions.explanation: A point is an exact location in space. It has no length, width, or height. It is represented by a dot and named with a capital letter (A, B, C...).

questions.question: How many straight lines can be drawn through two given points?
questions.explanation: Through any two points, exactly one straight line can be drawn. This is a fundamental geometry rule.
